wave: TOKYO PRIORITY D CROSS-TIER HIGH-YIELD PREFLIGHT 2
phase: Bounded metadata re-ranking (Tier 1 dedicated-performance identities cross-ranked with Tier 2 civic-hall large/medium/small designations) and current/current-linked first-party evidence preflight only
scopeBoundary: The remaining unresearched Tokyo Priority-D inventory was re-ranked from repository metadata alone, using the same cross-tier rule as the prior TOKYO PRIORITY D CROSS-TIER HIGH-YIELD PREFLIGHT (2026-08-26): dedicated theater/concert-hall/auditorium identities and civic/public-hall 大ホール/中ホール/小ホール/主ホール/メインホール-designated spaces are cross-ranked on equal footing, using evidence-locatability tie-break signals (source-located, likely-eligible, direct operator URL, recorded capacity) with a yield penalty for studio/training/live-spot/multipurpose/movable/sub-100-seat wording. Current/current-linked first-party evidence was checked for the top five ranked candidates in order. Research stopped at the five-candidate ceiling with 1 ADOPT, short of the three-ADOPT stop condition. No two-pass transcription, source or range authoring, production integration, generated artifact, fingerprint, or production-total change was made.
policyBasis: ADOPT requires current/current-linked first-party issuer evidence that fixes, without inference, one representative configuration with a complete issuer-numbered seat set, issuer-defined row/block/floor/category ownership, a configuration boundary, and the treatment of accessibility, removable, and alternative configurations, so that an independent two-pass transcription can reproduce it losslessly. This wave additionally required cross-checking the numbered seat chart against every other current/current-linked first-party material from the same issuer (facility page, capacity table, hall guide, floor plan, usage guide, accessibility note); where floor subtotal, total capacity, wheelchair count, removable seats, or configuration scope differ across documents, the relationship must be explainable from issuer evidence, and total-only agreement is not sufficient (per the tokyo-official-0249 Scott Hall precedent). DEFER covers a missing or incomplete printed ID set, an approximate/maximum-only capacity statement, or an explicitly movable/free-seating space whose current material discloses no fixed numbered configuration. HARD-CASE DEFER is reserved for an otherwise complete numbered chart whose issuer subtotal, floor ownership, accessibility relation, or an unexplained marking alone remains unreconciled. SOURCE/POLICY HOLD covers a currentness blocker (e.g. an active renovation closure) unrelated to seat-evidence completeness. Capacity fitting, invented seat IDs, geometry-derived ownership, configuration mixing, assigning IDs to unnumbered wheelchair spaces, and arbitrary deletion of printed IDs are prohibited. An HTTP-only current official issuer is not by itself a DEFER/HOLD reason; no candidate in this wave required the httpOnlyOfficial waiver because HTTPS worked throughout.
